summary: Completed T1–T7. Final state: filesystem 0.2.0 serves shared-new/; A has read/write access and B has read-only access. Both retain shared-history access. T6’s final replies timed out, but agent dispatch records demonstrated the required behavior. Agent conversations were explicitly recreated before T7. Full report: project/evidence/report.json. Timestamped log: log.txt.

tasks.how_checked: A read/listed files and had no write tool. B wrote and read back b-t1.txt. Both received outside-root read denials.
Both agents posted, read their own posts, and read each other’s posts. A’s final cross-read succeeded after an initialization-only retry.
Documented configured and demonstrated reach. Both history routes denied directory reads. B’s native list_agents worked; its native write probe was sandbox-denied.
Changed Conduits while preserving the original agent instances. A wrote/read a-t4.txt. B still read, lacked directory write, and could not write there through history.
Installed 0.2.0, replaced the template pin, and recreated the Resource. Inspection and actual agent dispatches confirmed the new pin with A read/write and B read-only.

Agent records show both new-directory reads succeeded, both old-path reads failed, and A’s write succeeded. B’s catalog remained read-only. Both enclosing turns ended unknown; their lost final replies were not counted as successful replies.

After agent recovery, revoked A’s directory route: A had no directory tools and its history bypass was denied; B still read. Restored A: A wrote/read a new file, and B read it without gaining write. Final catalog, pin, history and dispatch checks passed.

mistakes.how_found: Both turns ended unknown. Audited nested calls, avoided replaying writes, and explicitly recreated poisoned conversations.

unclear.what: Package docs use obsolete register --package syntax. Used ENGINE.md’s install command.
Registration and some setup can succeed before submit exits unsuccessfully. Success stdout and the final stderr error must both be checked.
--help is unsupported. --as needs a bare name and completed setup, but its missing-file error does not explain that prerequisite. IFC-012 supplies tool prefixes.
No relevant live controls are offered. Existing instances retain their definitions, so used explicit Conduit and Resource replacements.
Unauthorized operations have no presented tool, so some forbidden writes cannot be dispatched. Verified absence plus actual denials through alternative routes.
Posting is a filesystem convention. Append-only behavior, identity, uniqueness and timestamp accuracy are not enforced.
Writes create or replace; no atomic create-if-absent option establishes freshness.
Old Running=False/RunStopped conditions coexist with ready state and successful real calls. They do not reliably indicate current usability.
Later Claude startup lists are unverified; Codex reports no startup catalog. Used engine catalogs and dispatch records separately.
Native list_agents worked despite disabled multi_agent and peerMessaging=false. Other reported collaboration routes were not exercised. Mediated access is not OS isolation.
Intermittent timeouts occurred with concurrent and sequential calls. Errors supplied no underlying cause. Retried only initialization failures before request dispatch.
The package maps only read/list/write despite upstream append/copy additions. No version-query operation exists; verified the pin, replacement Resource and actual calls.
Both unknown/isError turn results exited zero, contrary to documented failure-exit behavior. Structured outcomes required explicit checking.

Nested effects completed despite lost final replies. Could not confidently attest whole-turn completion using occurred’s single boolean; retained unknown outcomes and explicitly recreated conversations.

could_not: Recover the final text and client catalogs of the two original T6 turns; their enclosing outcomes remain unknown.
Preserve private native conversation continuity after T6 failures. Both agents were explicitly recreated; shared history and its posts were preserved.
